questions.scenario: All tests pass with H2 in PostgreSQL mode, but the first deployment fails because a Flyway migration uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT and a JSONB column.
questions.question: What change to the test strategy prevents this?
options: Disable Flyway in tests
Add more unit tests with Mockito
Write separate migrations for H2 and PostgreSQL
Run integration tests against the same PostgreSQL version as production using Testcontainers
questions.explanation: In-memory databases only approximate PostgreSQL. Running migrations and queries against a real PostgreSQL container catches dialect, constraint and locking differences before production.

questions.scenario: A test configuration declares @Bean @ServiceConnection PostgreSQLContainer postgres().
questions.question: What does @ServiceConnection do?
options: It lets Spring Boot derive the DataSource URL, username and password from the running container automatically
It creates a production database connection pool
It mocks the database so no container is needed
It disables Flyway migrations
questions.explanation: Spring Boot creates connection details from the container, replacing manual @DynamicPropertySource wiring.

questions.scenario: A concurrency test runs 50 parallel transfers on virtual threads and then checks total balances. The test class is annotated with @Transactional.
questions.question: Why is this test unreliable?
options: Testcontainers does not support transactions
The test's transaction is rolled back and does not cover work done in other threads' transactions, so commits, locks and visibility do not behave as in production
Virtual threads cannot use JDBC
@Transactional makes tests run sequentially
questions.explanation: Test-managed rollback suits simple repository tests. Concurrency and transaction-boundary tests must let real transactions commit, with independent data or clean-up instead.

questions.scenario: An integration test publishes a TransferCompleted event and then calls Thread.sleep(3000) before asserting that the listener received it. It fails intermittently on CI.
questions.question: What is the better approach?
options: Run the test only locally
Increase the sleep to 30 seconds
Use Awaitility to poll for the condition with a timeout (for example up to 10 seconds)
Remove the assertion
questions.explanation: Fixed sleeps are either too short (flaky) or too long (slow). Polling until the condition holds, with an upper bound, is both fast and reliable.

questions.scenario: Developers complain that mvn test now takes six minutes because of Testcontainers tests.
questions.question: Which changes help? (Choose two.)
options: Start a new container in every test method
Use one shared test configuration so Spring's context cache reuses the same containers across classes
Name integration tests *IT and run them with the Failsafe plugin in mvn verify, keeping mvn test for fast unit tests
Replace every container with H2
questions.explanation: Separating phases keeps the inner loop fast, and sharing the context and containers avoids repeated start-up. Per-test containers are slow; H2 reintroduces dialect bugs.

questions.scenario: Several test classes each declare different @MockitoBean fields while also importing the shared Testcontainers configuration. The suite starts many Spring contexts.
questions.question: Why does this happen?
options: Spring caches only one context per JVM
Testcontainers forces a new context per class
@MockitoBean always disables caching
Each distinct combination of mock beans changes the context configuration, so Spring cannot reuse the cached context
questions.explanation: The context cache key includes bean overrides. Standardising them (or moving mocks into a shared configuration) lets classes share one context and one set of containers.

questions.scenario: Production runs PostgreSQL 17. A colleague uses postgres:latest in the test container.
questions.question: What is the risk?
options: Tests may silently run on a different major version from production; pin the same version tag
There is no risk; newer is always better
Testcontainers rejects the latest tag
The tests will run faster but less securely
questions.explanation: Tests should mirror production. A floating tag can change behaviour, defaults or extensions without any change in your code.
